ConStat (NeurIPS 2024) computes contamination effects via reference benchmark comparison (r²=0.94 with true effects) — fully black-box, validated on factual/classification benchmarks. LogProber (2024) estimates per-item Safe Scores from token log-probabilities. 'On The Fragility of Benchmark Contamination Detection in Reasoning Models' (ICLR 2026) shows RL post-training obscures contamination signals, motivating multi-indicator approaches. 'Quantifying Data Contamination in Psychometric Evaluations of LLMs' (arXiv:2510.07175) measures contamination in psychological scales (Big Five, PVQ-40) where LLMs are test-takers — detection only, no correction, no judge modeling, different evaluation setting. **IRT for LLMs (no joint judge + contamination):** PSN-IRT (AAAI 2026) applies neural 4PL IRT to benchmark evaluation. MFRM has been applied to compare 10 LLM raters with human experts (arXiv:2505.18486, May 2025) and to ChatGPT-4 essay scoring (RMAL 2024). **Gap:** No existing work jointly models judge severity and contamination susceptibility within a single psychometric calibration framework. Moreover, sequential application of existing methods (debias → decontaminate or vice versa) is theoretically biased due to the confounding between severity and contamination effects. DG-IRT's gating mechanism has never been adapted from educational cheating detection to LLM benchmark contamination.

## Approach
We propose a Gated Many-Facet Rasch Model (G-MFRM) that extends the standard MFRM with a DG-IRT-inspired contamination gating mechanism, using a three-stage estimation strategy that ensures identifiability.

**Why joint estimation, not sequential pipeline.** A naive two-stage approach (e.g., CyclicJudge → DCR) suffers from two theoretical problems: (a) Bias propagation — in the first stage, CyclicJudge's severity estimates absorb contamination-induced performance inflation (since it cannot distinguish genuine ability from contamination), producing biased "debiased scores"; DCR then operates on these biased inputs, underestimating contamination for models judged by strict judges and overestimating it for models judged by lenient ones. (b) No uncertainty propagation — the first stage's point estimates enter the second stage as fixed inputs, causing confidence intervals to undercover. Joint Bayesian estimation in a single likelihood function resolves both problems: d_j and c_n are simultaneously identified, and the full posterior naturally propagates uncertainty across all parameters.

**Model formulation.** The core log-odds model is:

  logit(P_nij) = θ_n − b_i − d_j + c_n · e_i

where θ_n is model ability, b_i is item difficulty, d_j is judge severity, c_n is per-model contamination susceptibility, and e_i is per-item exposure level. The multiplicative gating term c_n · e_i replaces an overparameterized per-(model,item) formulation: instead of N×I free parameters, this hierarchical decomposition requires only N + I parameters (or just N when e_i is externally anchored). **Three-stage estimation (resolving circularity).**

*Stage 1 — Standard 3-facet MFRM:* Fit θ_n, b_i, d_j via Bayesian MCMC (NumPyro on GPU), ignoring contamination. This produces initial ability estimates and person-fit statistics (lz, EMRi) per model.

*Stage 2 — External exposure estimation:* Estimate e_i from external proxies independent of the MFRM fit:

  (b) Temporal signals: performance gaps on items with pre-cutoff vs. post-cutoff variants.
  (c) LogProber Safe Scores: per-item memorization indicators from token log-probability analysis (gray-box; for models exposing logprobs).
  Indicators combined via weighted composite (weights tuned on held-out validation split) to produce ê_i. Person-fit statistics from Stage 1 serve as validation only — not used to estimate e_i, avoiding circularity.

*Stage 3 — Joint Gated MFRM:* Refit the full 4-facet model with ê_i as fixed covariates and c_n as latent parameters, using Stage 1 estimates as informative priors. Identifiability constraints: sum(c_n) = 0 and ê_i scale fixed from Stage 2. This yields contamination-corrected fair scores θ̂_n — model ability purged of both judge bias (d_j) and contamination inflation (c_n · ê_i).

**N-gram overlap handling.** Dropped for proprietary models (training data undisclosed). ConStat and temporal signals are fully black-box; LogProber requires only logprob access. For open-weight models (DeepSeek-V4, Kimi K2.6, Qwen3, Llama 4), n-gram overlap serves as supplementary validation of ê_i.

**Validation.** Primary benchmarks: Arena-Hard and WildBench (high discriminative power for 2026 frontier models). Supplementary benchmark: MT-Bench (included for continuity with prior work but with acknowledged ceiling effects for frontier models; score distributions reported transparently). Evaluated models (examinees): 15–20 LLMs spanning frontier proprietary (GPT-5.5, Claude Opus 4.7, Claude Sonnet 4.6, Gemini 2.5 Pro), frontier open-weight (DeepSeek-V4-Pro, Kimi K2.6, Qwen3-235B-A22B, Llama 4 Maverick), and mid-tier models (Qwen3.6-27B, Llama 4 Scout, Mistral Medium 3, DeepSeek-V4-Base, etc.) to ensure sufficient score variance for parameter estimation. LLM judges: 8 models (GPT-5.5, Claude Opus 4.7, Claude Sonnet 4.6, DeepSeek-V4-Pro, Kimi K2.6, Qwen3-235B-A22B, Qwen3.6-27B, Llama 4 Maverick). When a model serves as both judge and examinee, leave-one-out is applied: its own judgments are excluded from its examinee scoring, with sensitivity analysis of judge-examinee overlap effects.

Reference benchmark variants for ConStat constructed via GPT-5.5/Claude-assisted rephrasing with the equivalence validation protocol described above.

**Baselines (7 methods + naive pipeline):** (1) raw multi-judge averages, (2) CyclicJudge bias-only correction, (3) DCR Factor contamination-only adjustment, (4) Preference Leakage post-hoc calibration, (5) UDA neural K-factor Elo adjustment (converted to ranking for comparison), (6) Bias-Bounded Evaluation formal guarantee method, (7) Rogan-Gladen estimator (arXiv:2511.21140) as simple bias correction reference, and (8) naive two-stage pipeline (CyclicJudge → DCR).

**Evaluation metrics:** Primary: Kendall-τ rank correlation with held-out Chatbot Arena human votes. Secondary: Spearman-ρ, weighted Kendall-τ (τ_w, higher weight on top-rank discordance), top-k ranking accuracy (k=3, 5), pairwise accuracy vs. Chatbot Arena pairwise outcomes. Qualitative: per-model case study (2–3 models with largest G-MFRM correction) visualizing raw vs. corrected rankings and analyzing c_n estimates against known information. Where possible, category-specific correlation (coding, math, hard prompts) on Chatbot Arena sub-leaderboards.

**Ablations and additional analyses:** (a) Exposure indicator ablation: contribution of each signal (ConStat, temporal, LogProber) to ê_i. (b) **Multiplicative vs. additive gating ablation:** compare c_n · e_i (multiplicative interaction, proposed) against c_n + e_i (additive main effects, no interaction) to validate that the gating mechanism provides genuine improvement over simpler contamination control. (c) **Stage 3 joint refit contribution:** compare Stage 1+2 sequential estimates vs. Stage 3 joint estimates to quantify the marginal improvement from joint estimation — directly testing the core confounding claim. (d) Judge count sensitivity (2, 4, 6, 8 judges). (e) Facet fit statistics (infit/outfit MNSQ). (f) Person-fit validation: Stage 1 lz/EMRi flagging vs. Stage 3 c_n estimates. (g) Robustness to adversarial contamination per Wang et al. (ICLR 2026) fragility findings.

**Compute overhead and practical positioning.** We report an efficiency-improvement tradeoff table listing compute cost (API calls, GPU hours, human annotation hours) and Kendall-τ for each method. G-MFRM's overhead concentrates in the one-time reference benchmark construction (ConStat rephrasing + human validation); subsequent evaluation of new models requires only incremental MCMC fitting of new θ_n and c_n parameters. G-MFRM is positioned for high-stakes official leaderboard evaluation (e.g., Chatbot Arena) rather than routine model development, justifying the additional overhead for settings where ranking accuracy and interpretability matter most.

GPU hours: 180–250 (open-source judge inference via vLLM ~130h on A100-80GB; ConStat reference variant generation + evaluation ~30h; Bayesian MCMC fitting ~15h; ablations and sensitivity analysis ~50h; additional baselines UDA/Bias-Bounded ~25h). Casabianca & Beiting-Parrish (arXiv:2602.22585, Feb 2026) use MFRM to correct human rater severity effects in AI evaluation (OpenAI summarization dataset) but address human raters only, with no contamination modeling. 'Judging the Judges' (Soumik, arXiv:2604.23178, April 2026) empirically compares 9 debiasing strategies across 5 judges, finding style bias dominant (0.76–0.92) but explicitly lacks an explanatory measurement model. 'Bias and Uncertainty in LLM-as-a-Judge Estimation' (Fiedler, arXiv:2605.06939, May 2026) introduces formal J/delta-J diagnostics and identifies sign-reversal failure modes in shared-calibration comparisons, but stays within classical test theory without latent trait modeling. BiasScope (ICLR 2026) automates bias discovery post-hoc. Bias-Bounded Evaluation (arXiv:2603.05485, March 2026) provides formal (τ, δ)-bias-bounded guarantees retaining 61–99% ranking correlation on Arena-Hard-Auto. JudgeBiasBench (March 2026) defines a taxonomy of 12 bias types across 4 dimensions. UDA (AAAI 2026) uses neural K-factor adjustment to reduce inter-judge standard deviation by 63.4% in Elo-based pairwise evaluation. 'How to Correctly Report LLM-as-a-Judge Evaluations' (arXiv:2511.21140) applies the Rogan-Gladen (1978) estimator for bias correction under distribution shift in classification-based evaluation. **Contamination silo:** DCR Factor (EMNLP 2025) adjusts accuracy for contamination via fuzzy inference but ignores judge effects. Preference Leakage (ICLR 2026) quantifies generator-judge relatedness bias but proposes only post-hoc calibration. ConStat (NeurIPS 2024) computes contamination effects via reference benchmark comparison (r²=0.94 with true effects) — fully black-box, validated on factual/classification benchmarks. LogProber (2024) estimates per-item Safe Scores from token log-probabilities. 'On The Fragility of Benchmark Contamination Detection in Reasoning Models' (ICLR 2026) shows RL post-training obscures contamination signals, motivating multi-indicator approaches. 'Quantifying Data Contamination in Psychometric Evaluations of LLMs' (arXiv:2510.07175) measures contamination in psychological scales (Big Five, PVQ-40) where LLMs are test-takers — detection only, no correction, no judge modeling, different evaluation setting. **IRT for LLMs (no joint judge + contamination):** PSN-IRT (AAAI 2026) applies neural 4PL IRT to benchmark evaluation. MFRM has been applied to compare 10 LLM raters with human experts (arXiv:2505.18486, May 2025) and to ChatGPT-4 essay scoring (RMAL 2024). **Gap:** No existing work jointly models judge severity and contamination susceptibility within a single psychometric calibration framework. Moreover, sequential application of existing methods (debias → decontaminate or vice versa) is theoretically biased due to the confounding between severity and contamination effects. DG-IRT's gating mechanism has never been adapted from educational cheating detection to LLM benchmark contamination.

## Approach
We propose a Gated Many-Facet Rasch Model (G-MFRM) that extends the standard MFRM with a DG-IRT-inspired contamination gating mechanism, using a three-stage estimation strategy that ensures identifiability.

**Why joint estimation, not sequential pipeline.** A naive two-stage approach (e.g., CyclicJudge → DCR) suffers from two theoretical problems: (a) Bias propagation — in the first stage, CyclicJudge's severity estimates absorb contamination-induced performance inflation (since it cannot distinguish genuine ability from contamination), producing biased "debiased scores"; DCR then operates on these biased inputs, underestimating contamination for models judged by strict judges and overestimating it for models judged by lenient ones. (b) No uncertainty propagation — the first stage's point estimates enter the second stage as fixed inputs, causing confidence intervals to undercover. Joint Bayesian estimation in a single likelihood function resolves both problems: d_j and c_n are simultaneously identified, and the full posterior naturally propagates uncertainty across all parameters.

**Model formulation.** The core log-odds model is:

  logit(P_nij) = θ_n − b_i − d_j + c_n · e_i

where θ_n is model ability, b_i is item difficulty, d_j is judge severity, c_n is per-model contamination susceptibility, and e_i is per-item exposure level. The multiplicative gating term c_n · e_i replaces an overparameterized per-(model,item) formulation: instead of N×I free parameters, this hierarchical decomposition requires only N + I parameters (or just N when e_i is externally anchored). This follows the LLTM (Linear Logistic Test Model, Fischer 1973) tradition and is a rank-1 special case of AMMI decomposition, both with established identifiability guarantees.

The DG-IRT gating interpretation: when e_i ≈ 0 (unexposed item), the model reduces to the standard 3-facet MFRM measuring genuine ability; when e_i > 0, performance is inflated by c_n · e_i. This directly mirrors DG-IRT's decomposition of observed performance into genuine and cheating-inflated distributions, but with three domain-specific adaptations: (1) continuous e_i replacing DG-IRT's binary exposure indicator to capture graded contamination levels; (2) integration of the judge severity facet d_j absent from DG-IRT's single-rater setting; (3) external estimation of exposure status replacing DG-IRT's assumption of administrator-known exposure.

**Three-stage estimation (resolving circularity).**

*Stage 1 — Standard 3-facet MFRM:* Fit θ_n, b_i, d_j via Bayesian MCMC (NumPyro on GPU), ignoring contamination. This produces initial ability estimates and person-fit statistics (lz, EMRi) per model.

*Stage 2 — External exposure estimation:* Estimate e_i from external proxies independent of the MFRM fit:
  (a) ConStat delta scores: compare model performance on original benchmark items vs. rephrased/synthetic reference variants (fully black-box, validated r²=0.94 with true contamination effects). For open-ended generation benchmarks (Arena-Hard, WildBench), we address the rephrasing equivalence challenge through: task-specific checklist generation for original and rephrased prompts with ≥90% checklist overlap required; equivalence validation by ≥3 human annotators with Fleiss' κ ≥ 0.7; same judge panel scoring both variants to control judge noise; and a controlled validation study using known-contaminated open-weight models to verify ConStat delta scores reflect true contamination on open-ended tasks.
  (b) Temporal signals: performance gaps on items with pre-cutoff vs. post-cutoff variants.
  (c) LogProber Safe Scores: per-item memorization indicators from token log-probability analysis (gray-box; for models exposing logprobs).
  Indicators combined via weighted composite (weights tuned on held-out validation split) to produce ê_i. Person-fit statistics from Stage 1 serve as validation only — not used to estimate e_i, avoiding circularity.

*Stage 3 — Joint Gated MFRM:* Refit the full 4-facet model with ê_i as fixed covariates and c_n as latent parameters, using Stage 1 estimates as informative priors. Identifiability constraints: sum(c_n) = 0 and ê_i scale fixed from Stage 2. This yields contamination-corrected fair scores θ̂_n — model ability purged of both judge bias (d_j) and contamination inflation (c_n · ê_i).

**N-gram overlap handling.** Dropped for proprietary models (training data undisclosed). ConStat and temporal signals are fully black-box; LogProber requires only logprob access. For open-weight models (DeepSeek-V4, Kimi K2.6, Qwen3, Llama 4), n-gram overlap serves as supplementary validation of ê_i.

**Validation.** Primary benchmarks: Arena-Hard and WildBench (high discriminative power for 2026 frontier models). Supplementary benchmark: MT-Bench (included for continuity with prior work but with acknowledged ceiling effects for frontier models; score distributions reported transparently). Evaluated models (examinees): 15–20 LLMs spanning frontier proprietary (GPT-5.5, Claude Opus 4.7, Claude Sonnet 4.6, Gemini 2.5 Pro), frontier open-weight (DeepSeek-V4-Pro, Kimi K2.6, Qwen3-235B-A22B, Llama 4 Maverick), and mid-tier models (Qwen3.6-27B, Llama 4 Scout, Mistral Medium 3, DeepSeek-V4-Base, etc.) to ensure sufficient score variance for parameter estimation. LLM judges: 8 models (GPT-5.5, Claude Opus 4.7, Claude Sonnet 4.6, DeepSeek-V4-Pro, Kimi K2.6, Qwen3-235B-A22B, Qwen3.6-27B, Llama 4 Maverick). When a model serves as both judge and examinee, leave-one-out is applied: its own judgments are excluded from its examinee scoring, with sensitivity analysis of judge-examinee overlap effects.

Reference benchmark variants for ConStat constructed via GPT-5.5/Claude-assisted rephrasing with the equivalence validation protocol described above.

**Baselines (7 methods + naive pipeline):** (1) raw multi-judge averages, (2) CyclicJudge bias-only correction, (3) DCR Factor contamination-only adjustment, (4) Preference Leakage post-hoc calibration, (5) UDA neural K-factor Elo adjustment (converted to ranking for comparison), (6) Bias-Bounded Evaluation formal guarantee method, (7) Rogan-Gladen estimator (arXiv:2511.21140) as simple bias correction reference, and (8) naive two-stage pipeline (CyclicJudge → DCR).

**Evaluation metrics:** Primary: Kendall-τ rank correlation with held-out Chatbot Arena human votes. Secondary: Spearman-ρ, weighted Kendall-τ (τ_w, higher weight on top-rank discordance), top-k ranking accuracy (k=3, 5), pairwise accuracy vs. Chatbot Arena pairwise outcomes. Qualitative: per-model case study (2–3 models with largest G-MFRM correction) visualizing raw vs. corrected rankings and analyzing c_n estimates against known information. Where possible, category-specific correlation (coding, math, hard prompts) on Chatbot Arena sub-leaderboards.

**Ablations and additional analyses:** (a) Exposure indicator ablation: contribution of each signal (ConStat, temporal, LogProber) to ê_i. (b) Multiplicative vs. additive gating ablation: compare c_n · e_i (multiplicative interaction, proposed) against c_n + e_i (additive main effects, no interaction) to validate that the gating mechanism provides genuine improvement over simpler contamination control. (c) Stage 3 joint refit contribution: compare Stage 1+2 sequential estimates vs. Stage 3 joint estimates to quantify the marginal improvement from joint estimation — directly testing the core confounding claim. (d) Judge count sensitivity (2, 4, 6, 8 judges). (e) Facet fit statistics (infit/outfit MNSQ). (f) Person-fit validation: Stage 1 lz/EMRi flagging vs. Stage 3 c_n estimates. (g) Robustness to adversarial contamination per Wang et al. (ICLR 2026) fragility findings.

**Compute overhead and practical positioning.** We report an efficiency-improvement tradeoff table listing compute cost (API calls, GPU hours, human annotation hours) and Kendall-τ for each method. G-MFRM's overhead concentrates in the one-time reference benchmark construction (ConStat rephrasing + human validation); subsequent evaluation of new models requires only incremental MCMC fitting of new θ_n and c_n parameters. G-MFRM is positioned for high-stakes official leaderboard evaluation (e.g., Chatbot Arena) rather than routine model development, justifying the additional overhead for settings where ranking accuracy and interpretability matter most.

## Resource Estimate
GPU hours: 180–250 (open-source judge inference via vLLM ~130h on A100-80GB; ConStat reference variant generation + evaluation ~30h; Bayesian MCMC fitting ~15h; ablations and sensitivity analysis ~50h; additional baselines UDA/Bias-Bounded ~25h). Timeline: 10–12 weeks (G-MFRM implementation + ConStat integration 3w, reference benchmark construction + human equivalence validation 2w, multi-judge data collection 3w, experiments and analysis 2w, paper writing 2w). Estimated cost: $450–625 GPU (A100 spot) + ~$900–1200 proprietary judge API calls (GPT-5.5, Claude Opus 4.7, Claude Sonnet 4.6, Gemini 2.5 Pro).

## Inspired By
Cross-domain transfer of DG-IRT (Shu et al., Psychometrika 2013) gating mechanism from educational cheating detection to LLM contamination; MFRM multi-facet calibration for judge bias; LLTM (Fischer 1973) design-matrix decomposition for identifiable contamination parameterization; ConStat (NeurIPS 2024) external exposure indicators; Fiedler (arXiv:2605.06939) sign-reversal diagnostics as motivation for joint estimation.

【缺陷 1】
- 类别: 评估方案缺陷
- 问题: Proposal 的核心 ground truth 验证依赖 "Kendall-τ rank correlation with held-out Chatbot Arena human votes"，但存在两个严重的方法学问题：(1) **Chatbot Arena 的 category-specific Elo 数据当前覆盖 327 个模型，proposal 仅选 15-20 个 LLM**——在小样本下 Kendall-τ 的统计 power 很低（15 个模型的 Kendall-τ 95% CI 非常宽），很难检测到方法间 τ 差异是否统计显著。PSN-IRT 在 41,871 items 上才达到 τ=0.9048，而 G-MFRM 在 15-20 models 上即使 τ=0.90 vs baseline τ=0.85，其 confidence interval 的 overlap 可能导致结论不具统计意义。(2) **Chatbot Arena votes 本身包含 contamination 和 bias 效应**——如果一个模型在 Arena 中因 contamination 获得高 Elo，而 G-MFRM 正确地降低了该模型的排名，Kendall-τ 反而会下降。用可能 contaminated 的 ground truth 验证 decontamination 方法存在逻辑矛盾。
- 严重度: 可补救
- 补救方案: (1) **统计 power 分析**：报告在 15-20 models 样本量下，检测到特定 Kendall-τ 差异（如 Δτ=0.05）所需的 statistical power，使用 permutation test 或 bootstrap 95% CI 来报告方法间差异的统计显著性，而非仅报告点估计。(2) **补充 ground truth**：除 Chatbot Arena 外，增加一个 controlled ground truth：在 open-weight models 上构造 **known-contamination synthetic scenario**（故意在特定 benchmark items 上进行 fine-tuning 制造已知 contamination），验证 G-MFRM 能否正确恢复 pre-contamination ranking。这是 DCR 和 ConStat 论文都采用的 controlled contamination injection 方法论，是审稿人期望的标准验证手段。(3) **Arena sub-leaderboard 分析**：利用 Chatbot Arena 的 category-specific rankings (coding, math, hard prompts) 分别计算 τ，考察 G-MFRM 在不同类别上的改进是否一致。
- 调研依据: DCR Factor (EMNLP 2025) 使用 117 个 contamination-injected model variants 验证 adjusted accuracy；ConStat (NeurIPS 2024) 使用 controlled contamination 验证 r²=0.94；PSN-IRT (AAAI 2026) 在大规模 item pool 上计算 Kendall-τ。小样本 Kendall-τ 的统计 power 问题是计量心理学的基本常识。

【缺陷 2】
- 类别: 可行性问题
- 问题: **ConStat 在 open-ended generation benchmark 上的适用性未经验证，但 proposal 的 primary benchmark 恰好是 Arena-Hard 和 WildBench（open-ended generation）**。调研发现，ConStat (NeurIPS 2024) 的 r²=0.94 是在 **factual/classification benchmark** 上验证的；DCR Factor (EMNLP 2025) 同样在 SST-2/LIAR2/GSM8K 上验证。对于 open-ended generation tasks，"rephrased reference benchmark" 的语义等价性远比 factual QA 复杂——rephrased prompt 可能改变任务的创意空间、偏好倾向等。Proposal 虽然提到了 equivalence validation protocol（checklist overlap ≥90%, Fleiss' κ ≥ 0.7, ≥3 annotators），但这本身需要大量人工标注且**尚无先例**证明 ConStat 方法论能在 open-ended generation 上工作。这是 Stage 2 exposure estimation 的核心组件，如果 ConStat delta scores 在 open-ended tasks 上不可靠，整个 e_i 估计和下游的 c_n 估计都会受影响。
- 严重度: 可补救
- 补救方案: (1) **单独设计一个 ConStat validity study 作为实验的前置步骤**：在 2-3 个已知有 contamination 的 open-weight models 上，构造 Arena-Hard/WildBench 的 rephrased variants，验证 ConStat delta scores 是否能区分 contaminated vs. clean models。如果 r² 显著低于 factual benchmark 上的 0.94，需要透明报告并讨论 limitation。(2) **增加 temporal signal 和 LogProber 在 e_i 估计中的权重**：如果 ConStat 在 open-ended tasks 上表现不佳，proposal 应准备好一个 **fallback 方案**，即主要依赖 temporal pre/post-cutoff signals 和 LogProber Safe Scores，将 ConStat 降级为辅助验证。(3) **在 ablation 中已经包含了 exposure indicator ablation**（贡献拆解），这很好，但应额外报告 e_i 估计的 **inter-indicator agreement**（ConStat vs. temporal vs. LogProber 之间的相关性），让读者判断各信号是否 converge。
- 调研依据: ConStat (NeurIPS 2024) 论文明确在 factual/classification benchmark 上验证；DCR (EMNLP 2025) 同样限于 classification/reasoning benchmarks。Open-ended generation 的 rephrasing equivalence 是一个 open problem。

- 类别: baseline 不足或过时
- 问题: Baseline 列表中的 **UDA** 是 pairwise Elo-based 方法，proposal 提到 "converted to ranking for comparison"，但这个转换本身不 trivial：UDA 的 K-factor adjustment 在 pairwise comparison 框架内操作，而 G-MFRM 在 pointwise scoring 框架内操作。两种 evaluation paradigm 的直接比较（即使通过 ranking 转换）是否公平，需要明确说明。另外，**缺少一个重要的 baseline**：**简单 IRT 模型（如 2PL 或 PSN-IRT 的 4PL）不带 judge facet 也不带 contamination facet**，仅估计 ability 和 difficulty。这是验证 G-MFRM 各 facet 边际贡献的最基本参照——如果连 vanilla IRT 都无法对比，审稿人无法判断 MFRM 的 judge facet 和 contamination gating 各自贡献了多少。
- 严重度: 可补救
- 补救方案: (1) **增加 vanilla IRT baseline**（2PL 或 Rasch 模型，无 judge facet 无 contamination）作为最基本参照。这样 baseline 梯度为：vanilla IRT → 3-facet MFRM (Stage 1) → G-MFRM (Stage 3)，可以清晰展示每个组件的 marginal contribution。(2) **明确 UDA 转换方法**：详细说明如何将 UDA 的 Elo-based pairwise evaluation 转换为与 G-MFRM 可比的 ranking/score，讨论这种转换是否引入额外 bias，或考虑在 pairwise evaluation 框架下也对 G-MFRM 做一次评估（将 G-MFRM 的 θ̂_n 转换为 pairwise win probability 预测，与 Arena pairwise outcomes 比较）。(3) 考虑增加 **Rogan-Gladen estimator** (arXiv:2511.21140) 作为 simple bias correction baseline（proposal 中已有这个，很好）。

- 类别: ablation 不完整
- 问题: Proposal 中 ablation (c) "Stage 3 joint refit contribution: compare Stage 1+2 sequential estimates vs. Stage 3 joint estimates" 是验证核心 claim（joint estimation 优于 sequential estimation）的**最关键实验**，但设计不够充分。当前仅比较 "Stage 1+2 sequential" vs. "Stage 3 joint"，但 sequential 的**顺序效应**（debias→decontaminate vs. decontaminate→debias）未被测试。Proposal 的核心 claim 是 sequential approach 有 bias propagation，且 Fiedler (arXiv:2605.06939) 已记录了 sign-reversal 问题——如果不测试两种 sequential 顺序并展示它们产生不同（甚至 sign-reversed）结果，而 joint estimation 不受此影响，就无法充分支撑 "methodologically necessary" 的核心 claim。
- 严重度: 可补救
- 补救方案: 将 ablation (c) 扩展为三组比较：(i) Sequential A: CyclicJudge debias → DCR decontaminate, (ii) Sequential B: DCR decontaminate → CyclicJudge debias, (iii) Joint G-MFRM (Stage 3)。报告三者的 Kendall-τ 和 per-model ranking 差异，特别关注是否存在 Sequential A 和 Sequential B 产生 **不同排名** 的 case（即 order-dependence），以及 G-MFRM 是否消除了这种 order-dependence。这直接对应 Fiedler 的 sign-reversal 发现，是最有说服力的证据。

【发掘 agent 本轮输出】:
Now I have sufficient research to make my assessment. Let me compile my analysis.

---

【状态】: 有发掘空间

【前置调研发现】
- [Comparing Human and AI Rater Effects Using the Many-Facet Rasch Model](https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.18486) (arXiv, May 2025): 将 MFRM 应用于 LLM rater，但仅做诊断性分析（rater effects 对比），不做 contamination 建模，也不做 correction。与本 proposal 关系：直接前驱工作，proposal 的 MFRM 部分可以视为此工作的延伸，但核心 novelty 不冲突。
- [Correcting Human Labels for Rater Effects in AI Evaluation](https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.22585) (arXiv, Feb 2026): Casabianca & Beiting-Parrish 用 MFRM 修正人类标注者的 severity/leniency effects，但聚焦 human rater（非 LLM judge），且无 contamination 建模。与本 proposal 的区别明确。
- [Bias and Uncertainty in LLM-as-a-Judge Estimation](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.06939) (arXiv, May 2026): Fiedler 识别 shared-calibration comparison 的 sign-reversal failure mode，停留在 classical test theory 层面（J/δ-J 诊断），未引入 latent trait model。本 proposal 将其定位为"sequential estimation bias 的症状"较为恰当。
- [Preference Leakage: A Contamination Problem in LLM-as-a-judge](https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.01534) (ICLR 2026): 量化 generator-judge relatedness 导致的 bias，提出 post-hoc calibration 但无结构化 psychometric 模型。属于 contamination silo 的代表工作。
- [Judging the Judges](https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.23178) (arXiv, April 2026): 9 种 debiasing 策略的实证比较，发现 style bias 远超 position bias，但明确缺乏 explanatory measurement model。
- [DCR Factor](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2507.11405) (EMNLP 2025): 用 fuzzy inference 调整 contamination，忽略 judge effects。
- [ConStat](https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.16281) (NeurIPS 2024): 通过 reference benchmark 比较检测+量化 contamination（r²=0.94），完全 black-box。核心工具组件，但非竞争性工作。
- [UDA](https://ojs.aaai.org/index.php/AAAI/article/view/40788) (AAAI 2026): 用 neural K-factor 在 Elo 系统中做无监督 debiasing，减少 inter-judge standard deviation 63.4%。方法论层面与本 proposal 完全不同（neural Elo vs. psychometric MFRM）。
- [Using Deterministic, Gated IRT Model to Detect Test Cheating](https://www.cambridge.org/core/journals/psychometrika/article/abs/using-deterministic-gated-item-response-theory-model-to-detect-test-cheating-due-to-item-compromise/34FE98C0FA7367881713D0019619E53E) (Psychometrika 2013): DG-IRT 原始论文，binary exposure indicator，single-rater setting，administrator-known exposure。本 proposal 的 gating 机制直接源于此。

- **调研总结**: 这个领域当前的研究者在 judge bias 和 contamination 两个方向上高度活跃但割裂工作——bias 方向在探索各种 debiasing 策略（round-robin、neural Elo、formal bounds），contamination 方向在改进检测和量化（reference benchmark、temporal signal、logprob analysis），但**确实没有人在单一 psychometric 框架内做 joint estimation**。这个 gap 是真实存在的。领域趋势是从 ad-hoc correction 走向 principled measurement framework（MFRM for rater effects, IRT for item analysis），但融合二者并加入 contamination facet 尚未有人做。

---

【发掘点 1】
- 维度: 核心 claim 强化
- 内容: Proposal 的核心 claim 是"joint estimation is methodologically necessary, not merely convenient"——这是整篇论文最有力的 selling point，但当前论述主要依赖直觉性论证（"第一步的误差作为第二步的输入"），缺乏 **formal statement**。建议在 approach 中增加一个简短但严格的 **confounding theorem 或 proposition**：在定义清晰的条件下（如 d_j 和 c_n·e_i 在 item 子集上的共变结构满足某种非正交条件），证明 sequential two-stage estimator 的 θ̂_n 是 asymptotically biased 的，且 bias 方向取决于 d_j 与 c_n·e_i 的协方差符号。这不需要是完整的 proof（可以放 appendix），但即使是一个 semi-formal proposition with proof sketch，也会让"methodologically necessary"这个 claim 从 rhetoric 升级为 result。Fiedler (2605.06939) 已经在 classical test theory 层面识别了 sign-reversal failure mode，你可以将其 formalize 为 sequential estimation bias 的一个 corollary。
- 价值: 这直接命中 Novelty 和 Significance。审稿人对"我们是第一个做 X"这种 claim 天然怀疑；但如果你能证明"不做 X 必然导致 bias"，这就把 novelty 从 "first to integrate" 升级为 "identify and resolve a previously uncharacterized estimation pathology"。后者远比前者有说服力。
- 调研依据: Fiedler (arXiv:2605.06939) 的 sign-reversal failure mode 提供了 empirical motivation；IRT 文献中关于 omitted facet bias 的经典结果（如 Rasch model misspecification literature）可以作为 formal argument 的起点。

【发掘点 2】
- 维度: significance 提升
- 内容: 当前 proposal 将 G-MFRM 定位为"high-stakes official leaderboard evaluation (e.g., Chatbot Arena)"。这个定位可以进一步强化：不仅仅是 ranking correction，更是**评估方法论的范式转移**——从"先检测 contamination、再修正 bias"的 pipeline 思维，到"将所有 measurement artifacts 纳入统一 generative model"的 psychometric 思维。Proposal 可以更明确地 argue：当前 LLM evaluation 领域正在经历从 ad-hoc metrics 到 principled measurement 的转型（evidence: MFRM 开始被用于 LLM raters [2505.18486]、IRT 被用于 benchmark analysis [PSN-IRT, AAAI 2026]、Fiedler 引入 formal bias diagnostics），G-MFRM 是这一趋势的自然 culmination——**第一个将所有已识别的 measurement artifacts（judge bias + contamination + item difficulty）统一在单一 generative model 中的框架**。这个 framing 比"我们 jointly estimate 四个 facets"更有 narrative force。
- 价值: 命中 Significance。审稿人判断 significance 时关注的不仅是"这个方法多好"，更是"这篇论文改变了领域怎么思考问题"。如果 G-MFRM 仅被呈现为一个更好的方法，significance 有上限；如果被呈现为一种新的评估范式（统一 generative model for all measurement artifacts），narrative impact 大幅提升。
- 调研依据: 基于领域整体趋势判断——2505.18486 将 MFRM 引入 LLM evaluation，PSN-IRT (AAAI 2026) 将 neural IRT 引入 benchmark analysis，Fiedler (2605.06939) 引入 formal diagnostics——这些都指向领域正在从 ad-hoc 走向 principled measurement，G-MFRM 可以定位为这一趋势的 integrative milestone。

【发掘点 3】
- 维度: novelty 锐化
- 内容: Proposal 中 DG-IRT → LLM contamination 的 cross-domain transfer 已经列出了三个 domain-specific adaptations（continuous e_i、MFRM d_j integration、external anchoring pipeline）。但当前叙述中，这三个 adaptation 被平等罗列，缺乏**层次感**。建议将第三个 adaptation（external exposure estimation）提升为**核心 methodological contribution** 而非仅仅是 adaptation。原因：DG-IRT 的最大假设是"exposure status is known to the administrator"——这在教育测试中合理（管理员知道哪些题目泄露了），但在 LLM benchmark contamination 中根本不成立（没人知道哪个 model 在训练时见过哪些 benchmark items）。因此，整个 Stage 2 external anchoring pipeline 不是一个"适应性修改"，而是**解决了 DG-IRT 框架在 LLM domain 中最根本的不可行性**。将其提升为 core contribution 会让 novelty narrative 更加锐利：不是"我们把 A 方法用到了 B 领域"（incremental），而是"A 方法在 B 领域有一个根本性障碍，我们设计了解决方案"（non-trivial）。
- 价值: 命中 Novelty。"Cross-domain transfer" 在审稿人眼中经常被视为 incremental（"applying method X to domain Y"）。但如果你能 argue 这个 transfer 要求解决一个 non-trivial obstacle——原方法的核心假设在新 domain 不成立——那就将 contribution 从 application 升级为 methodological innovation。
- 调研依据: DG-IRT 原始论文 (Shu, Henson & Luecht, Psychometrika 2013) 明确假设 exposure status 由 administrator 提供。ConStat (NeurIPS 2024) 提供了 black-box exposure estimation 工具，但将其整合到 IRT 框架的 estimation pipeline 中是本 proposal 的独立 contribution。

【发掘点 4】
- 维度: related work 差异化
- 内容: Proposal 当前的 related work 覆盖非常全面，但有一个潜在的差异化弱点需要主动防御：**Preference Leakage (ICLR 2026)** 的 calibration 方法。Preference Leakage 的核心发现是 generator-judge relatedness 导致 systematic bias，并提出了 calibration 方法（auto-calibration、contextual calibration 等）。一个 shrewd reviewer 可能会问："Preference Leakage 的 relatedness bias 不就是一种 contamination 吗？他们的 calibration 不就是在做类似的 correction 吗？" Proposal 需要更明确地 articulate 二者的区别：(a) Preference Leakage 的 contamination 是 **judge-side** 的（judge 因为与 generator 相关而 bias），而 G-MFRM 的 contamination 是 **examinee-side** 的（model 因为在训练中见过 benchmark items 而 performance inflate）——这是两种完全不同的 contamination 机制；(b) Preference Leakage 的 calibration 是 post-hoc adjustment 而非 joint generative modeling；(c) 实际上 Preference Leakage 识别的 relatedness bias 可以被 G-MFRM 的 d_j facet 部分捕获（如果用 related model 做 judge，其 severity shift 会反映在 d_j 中）。建议在 related work 中增加这一明确的差异化论述。
- 价值: 命中 Related Work 差异化。Preference Leakage 是 ICLR 2026 工作，知名度高，reviewer 大概率会想到这篇。如果 proposal 不主动 articulate 差异，reviewer 可能会认为 novelty 被部分覆盖。
- 调研依据: Preference Leakage (arXiv:2502.01534, ICLR 2026) 的核心发现是 generator-judge relatedness 导致 evaluation bias，与本 proposal 的 contamination facet 在表面上有相似性，但机制完全不同。

【发掘点 5】
- 维度: 前提假设质疑
- 内容: G-MFRM 的 contamination gating term 是 **c_n · e_i**——一个 rank-1 multiplicative decomposition，假设 contamination 的效果可以分解为 per-model susceptibility 和 per-item exposure 的简单乘积。这个假设的前提是：一个 model 对所有 contaminated items 的 susceptibility 是同质的（只有一个标量 c_n），且一个 item 对所有 contaminated models 的 exposure level 是同质的（只有一个标量 e_i）。然而，现实中 contamination susceptibility 可能是**非同质的**——同一模型可能对 coding tasks 高度 contaminated 但对 reasoning tasks 几乎未 contaminated（因为不同 training data sources 覆盖不同 domain）。这意味着 rank-1 assumption 可能是一个 mis-specification。Proposal 应该**主动承认这一简化假设并讨论其后果**：(a) 在什么条件下 rank-1 is a good approximation（例如当 contamination 主要来自单一数据源时），(b) rank-1 misspecification 的 bias 方向是什么，(c) 是否可以通过 person-fit diagnostics（infit/outfit）检测 rank-1 violation。主动讨论比被 reviewer 指出后再辩护要好得多——这体现了对方法论限制的 intellectual honesty，反而会提升 paper 的可信度。
- 价值: 命中 Novelty（通过展示对 assumption 的深入理解来强化方法论的 rigor），也预防了 reviewer 的 "strong assumption" attack。Proposal 目前提到了 LLTM 和 AMMI 的 identifiability guarantee，但没有讨论 rank-1 assumption 何时会 break down。这是一个潜在的 reviewer attack surface——但如果 proposal 主动处理，反而变成展示 methodological maturity 的机会。
- 调研依据: 基于领域整体趋势判断。AMMI decomposition 文献（agricultural statistics 起源）广泛讨论了 rank 选择问题。IRT 文献中 multidimensional IRT vs. unidimensional IRT 的 misspecification literature 也与此相关。此外，Wang et al. (ICLR 2026) 关于 RL post-training 模糊 contamination signals 的发现暗示 contamination 的异质性。

- [Comparing Human and AI Rater Effects Using the Many-Facet Rasch Model](https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.18486)
- [Correcting Human Labels for Rater Effects in AI Evaluation](https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.22585)
- [Bias and Uncertainty in LLM-as-a-Judge Estimation](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.06939)
- [Preference Leakage: A Contamination Problem in LLM-as-a-judge](https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.01534)
- [Judging the Judges](https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.23178)
- [ConStat: Performance-Based Contamination Detection in Large Language Models](https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.16281)
- [UDA: Unsupervised Debiasing Alignment for Pair-wise LLM-as-a-Judge](https://ojs.aaai.org/index.php/AAAI/article/view/40788)
- [CyclicJudge: Mitigating Judge Bias Efficiently in LLM-based Evaluation](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2603.01865)
- [Towards Provably Unbiased LLM Judges via Bias-Bounded Evaluation](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2603.05485)
- [How to Correctly Report LLM-as-a-Judge Evaluations](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2511.21140)
- [Using Deterministic, Gated IRT Model to Detect Test Cheating](https://www.cambridge.org/core/journals/psychometrika/article/abs/using-deterministic-gated-item-response-theory-model-to-detect-test-cheating-due-to-item-compromise/34FE98C0FA7367881713D0019619E53E)
- [On The Fragility of Benchmark Contamination Detection in Reasoning Models](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2510.02386)
- [Quantifying Data Contamination in Psychometric Evaluations of LLMs](https://arxiv.org/html/2510.07175v1)

【补救 agent 本轮输出】:
Now I have sufficient research context. Let me synthesize my findings and produce the evaluation.

---

【状态】: 有缺陷待补救

【前置调研发现】
- **CyclicJudge (arXiv:2603.01865, March 2026)**: 实验在 MT-Bench 和临床 benchmark (MindEval) 上进行，使用 variance decomposition（scenario/generation/judge/residual），对比 baseline 包括 raw average、single-judge、random allocation 等。关键指标为 variance reduction 和 ranking stability，而非与 Chatbot Arena 的 Kendall-τ 相关性。
- **DCR Factor (EMNLP 2025)**: 在 SST-2、LIAR2、GSM8K 三个 benchmark 上测试，9 个 LLM (0.5B-72B)，117 个 contamination-injected model variants；验证指标为 adjusted accuracy 与 uncontaminated baseline 的误差 (~4%)。其实验完全基于 **classification/reasoning** benchmark，**未测试 open-ended generation** benchmark。
- **ConStat (NeurIPS 2024)**: 在 factual/classification benchmark 上验证 r²=0.94；完全 black-box；但论文本身 **未在 open-ended generation benchmark (如 Arena-Hard/WildBench) 上验证**。
- **Preference Leakage (ICLR 2026)**: 实验覆盖多个 LLM baseline 和 benchmark，发现 contextual calibration 最有效 (Error Bias 17.8→7.3)；使用 BERT classifier 验证 preference leakage 的可检测性 (82.4% accuracy)。
- **Bias-Bounded Evaluation (arXiv:2603.05485, March 2026)**: Arena-Hard-Auto 上 4 个 LLM judge 实验，61-99% ranking correlation 保持率，使用 (τ, δ)-bias-bounded formal guarantees。
- **UDA (AAAI 2026)**: 使用 neural K-factor 在 Elo-based pairwise evaluation 中减少 inter-judge standard deviation 63.4%，完全在 **pairwise** 评估框架内运作。
- **MFRM for LLM raters (arXiv:2505.18486, May 2025)**: 10 个 LLM + human raters 在 essay scoring 上比较，使用 Cronbach Alpha、Quadratic Weighted Kappa、infit/outfit MNSQ 等指标。
- **PSN-IRT (AAAI 2026)**: 11 个 benchmark / 41,871 items，与 Chatbot Arena 的 Kendall-τ 最高达 0.9048。
- **DG-IRT (Psychometrika 2013)**: 使用 hierarchical MCMC 估计，binary exposure indicators，在 educational testing data 上验证。其 identifiability 依赖于 known exposure status。
- **Chatbot Arena 2026**: 当前有 327 个模型，5.8M+ votes，支持 category-specific 排名（Overall, Coding, Math, Creative Writing, Hard Prompts 等）。
- **调研总结**: 这个领域的实验设计标准要求 (1) 与 Chatbot Arena human votes 的排名相关性作为核心 ground truth 验证，(2) 多个 baseline 的 compute-normalized 比较，(3) 充分的 ablation 隔离各组件贡献，(4) 对 open-ended generation benchmark 的适用性需要特别论证（现有 contamination 检测工具主要在 factual/classification benchmark 上验证）。审稿人普遍关注 identifiability、convergence diagnostics、以及方法的实际 ranking improvement margin。

---

【缺陷 1】
- 类别: 评估方案缺陷
- 问题: Proposal 的核心 ground truth 验证依赖 "Kendall-τ rank correlation with held-out Chatbot Arena human votes"，但存在两个严重的方法学问题：(1) **Chatbot Arena 的 category-specific Elo 数据当前覆盖 327 个模型，proposal 仅选 15-20 个 LLM**——在小样本下 Kendall-τ 的统计 power 很低（15 个模型的 Kendall-τ 95% CI 非常宽），很难检测到方法间 τ 差异是否统计显著。PSN-IRT 在 41,871 items 上才达到 τ=0.9048，而 G-MFRM 在 15-20 models 上即使 τ=0.90 vs baseline τ=0.85，其 confidence interval 的 overlap 可能导致结论不具统计意义。(2) **Chatbot Arena votes 本身包含 contamination 和 bias 效应**——如果一个模型在 Arena 中因 contamination 获得高 Elo，而 G-MFRM 正确地降低了该模型的排名，Kendall-τ 反而会下降。用可能 contaminated 的 ground truth 验证 decontamination 方法存在逻辑矛盾。
- 严重度: 可补救
- 补救方案: (1) **统计 power 分析**：报告在 15-20 models 样本量下，检测到特定 Kendall-τ 差异（如 Δτ=0.05）所需的 statistical power，使用 permutation test 或 bootstrap 95% CI 来报告方法间差异的统计显著性，而非仅报告点估计。(2) **补充 ground truth**：除 Chatbot Arena 外，增加一个 controlled ground truth：在 open-weight models 上构造 **known-contamination synthetic scenario**（故意在特定 benchmark items 上进行 fine-tuning 制造已知 contamination），验证 G-MFRM 能否正确恢复 pre-contamination ranking。这是 DCR 和 ConStat 论文都采用的 controlled contamination injection 方法论，是审稿人期望的标准验证手段。(3) **Arena sub-leaderboard 分析**：利用 Chatbot Arena 的 category-specific rankings (coding, math, hard prompts) 分别计算 τ，考察 G-MFRM 在不同类别上的改进是否一致。
- 调研依据: DCR Factor (EMNLP 2025) 使用 117 个 contamination-injected model variants 验证 adjusted accuracy；ConStat (NeurIPS 2024) 使用 controlled contamination 验证 r²=0.94；PSN-IRT (AAAI 2026) 在大规模 item pool 上计算 Kendall-τ。小样本 Kendall-τ 的统计 power 问题是计量心理学的基本常识。

【缺陷 2】
- 类别: 可行性问题
- 问题: **ConStat 在 open-ended generation benchmark 上的适用性未经验证，但 proposal 的 primary benchmark 恰好是 Arena-Hard 和 WildBench（open-ended generation）**。调研发现，ConStat (NeurIPS 2024) 的 r²=0.94 是在 **factual/classification benchmark** 上验证的；DCR Factor (EMNLP 2025) 同样在 SST-2/LIAR2/GSM8K 上验证。对于 open-ended generation tasks，"rephrased reference benchmark" 的语义等价性远比 factual QA 复杂——rephrased prompt 可能改变任务的创意空间、偏好倾向等。Proposal 虽然提到了 equivalence validation protocol（checklist overlap ≥90%, Fleiss' κ ≥ 0.7, ≥3 annotators），但这本身需要大量人工标注且**尚无先例**证明 ConStat 方法论能在 open-ended generation 上工作。这是 Stage 2 exposure estimation 的核心组件，如果 ConStat delta scores 在 open-ended tasks 上不可靠，整个 e_i 估计和下游的 c_n 估计都会受影响。
- 严重度: 可补救
- 补救方案: (1) **单独设计一个 ConStat validity study 作为实验的前置步骤**：在 2-3 个已知有 contamination 的 open-weight models 上，构造 Arena-Hard/WildBench 的 rephrased variants，验证 ConStat delta scores 是否能区分 contaminated vs. clean models。如果 r² 显著低于 factual benchmark 上的 0.94，需要透明报告并讨论 limitation。(2) **增加 temporal signal 和 LogProber 在 e_i 估计中的权重**：如果 ConStat 在 open-ended tasks 上表现不佳，proposal 应准备好一个 **fallback 方案**，即主要依赖 temporal pre/post-cutoff signals 和 LogProber Safe Scores，将 ConStat 降级为辅助验证。(3) **在 ablation 中已经包含了 exposure indicator ablation**（贡献拆解），这很好，但应额外报告 e_i 估计的 **inter-indicator agreement**（ConStat vs. temporal vs. LogProber 之间的相关性），让读者判断各信号是否 converge。
- 调研依据: ConStat (NeurIPS 2024) 论文明确在 factual/classification benchmark 上验证；DCR (EMNLP 2025) 同样限于 classification/reasoning benchmarks。Open-ended generation 的 rephrasing equivalence 是一个 open problem。

【缺陷 3】
- 类别: baseline 不足或过时
- 问题: Baseline 列表中的 **UDA** 是 pairwise Elo-based 方法，proposal 提到 "converted to ranking for comparison"，但这个转换本身不 trivial：UDA 的 K-factor adjustment 在 pairwise comparison 框架内操作，而 G-MFRM 在 pointwise scoring 框架内操作。两种 evaluation paradigm 的直接比较（即使通过 ranking 转换）是否公平，需要明确说明。另外，**缺少一个重要的 baseline**：**简单 IRT 模型（如 2PL 或 PSN-IRT 的 4PL）不带 judge facet 也不带 contamination facet**，仅估计 ability 和 difficulty。这是验证 G-MFRM 各 facet 边际贡献的最基本参照——如果连 vanilla IRT 都无法对比，审稿人无法判断 MFRM 的 judge facet 和 contamination gating 各自贡献了多少。
- 严重度: 可补救
- 补救方案: (1) **增加 vanilla IRT baseline**（2PL 或 Rasch 模型，无 judge facet 无 contamination）作为最基本参照。这样 baseline 梯度为：vanilla IRT → 3-facet MFRM (Stage 1) → G-MFRM (Stage 3)，可以清晰展示每个组件的 marginal contribution。(2) **明确 UDA 转换方法**：详细说明如何将 UDA 的 Elo-based pairwise evaluation 转换为与 G-MFRM 可比的 ranking/score，讨论这种转换是否引入额外 bias，或考虑在 pairwise evaluation 框架下也对 G-MFRM 做一次评估（将 G-MFRM 的 θ̂_n 转换为 pairwise win probability 预测，与 Arena pairwise outcomes 比较）。(3) 考虑增加 **Rogan-Gladen estimator** (arXiv:2511.21140) 作为 simple bias correction baseline（proposal 中已有这个，很好）。
- 调研依据: PSN-IRT (AAAI 2026) 使用 4PL IRT 作为基础模型与 Chatbot Arena 对比，Kendall-τ 可达 0.9048。这是该领域的标准 IRT baseline。

【缺陷 4】
- 类别: ablation 不完整
- 问题: Proposal 中 ablation (c) "Stage 3 joint refit contribution: compare Stage 1+2 sequential estimates vs. Stage 3 joint estimates" 是验证核心 claim（joint estimation 优于 sequential estimation）的**最关键实验**，但设计不够充分。当前仅比较 "Stage 1+2 sequential" vs. "Stage 3 joint"，但 sequential 的**顺序效应**（debias→decontaminate vs. decontaminate→debias）未被测试。Proposal 的核心 claim 是 sequential approach 有 bias propagation，且 Fiedler (arXiv:2605.06939) 已记录了 sign-reversal 问题——如果不测试两种 sequential 顺序并展示它们产生不同（甚至 sign-reversed）结果，而 joint estimation 不受此影响，就无法充分支撑 "methodologically necessary" 的核心 claim。
- 严重度: 可补救
- 补救方案: 将 ablation (c) 扩展为三组比较：(i) Sequential A: CyclicJudge debias → DCR decontaminate, (ii) Sequential B: DCR decontaminate → CyclicJudge debias, (iii) Joint G-MFRM (Stage 3)。报告三者的 Kendall-τ 和 per-model ranking 差异，特别关注是否存在 Sequential A 和 Sequential B 产生 **不同排名** 的 case（即 order-dependence），以及 G-MFRM 是否消除了这种 order-dependence。这直接对应 Fiedler 的 sign-reversal 发现，是最有说服力的证据。
- 调研依据: Fiedler (arXiv:2605.06939, May 2026) 明确记录了 sequential shared-calibration 的 sign-reversal failure modes。展示 sequential order-dependence 是验证 joint estimation necessity 的标准方法论。

【缺陷 5】
- 类别: 实验设计不足
- 问题: **MCMC convergence diagnostics 和 identifiability 验证在 proposal 中完全缺失**。Proposal 提到 "Bayesian MCMC in NumPyro" 和 "identifiability constraints: sum(c_n) = 0 and ê_i scale fixed"，但未说明如何验证 MCMC 收敛（R̂、ESS、trace plots）和参数 identifiability。IRT/MFRM 的 Bayesian estimation 在 LLM evaluation 场景中面临特殊挑战（near-constant responses from ceiling-effect models、collinearity between θ_n 和 c_n when e_i is uncertain），调研发现 arXiv:2605.07046 明确指出 IRT 在 LLM evaluation 中的 "singular data configurations" 问题。如果 MCMC 不收敛或参数不可辨识，整个方法论无效。
- 严重度: 可补救
- 补救方案: (1) **明确列出 convergence diagnostic protocol**：报告 R̂ < 1.01、ESS > 400（或相应标准）、trace plots 和 posterior predictive checks。(2) **参数恢复模拟（parameter recovery simulation）**：在提交论文前，先用 **known ground-truth parameters** 生成合成数据（已知 θ_n, b_i, d_j, c_n, e_i），验证 G-MFRM 能否准确恢复这些参数（mean absolute error、coverage of 95% credible intervals）。这是 psychometric modeling 论文的标准验证步骤，审稿人几乎一定会要求。(3) **特别测试边界情况**：当 e_i 全部接近 0（低 contamination 场景）或 c_n variance 很小时，c_n 是否仍可辨识；当模型数 N 较少（如 10 个）时，参数恢复是否退化。
- 调研依据: arXiv:2605.07046 指出 IRT 在 LLM evaluation 中的 numerical instability 问题；DG-IRT (Psychometrika 2013) 使用 hierarchical MCMC 并报告了 convergence diagnostics；NumPyro IRT 文献 (PMC 2023) 明确比较了 pystan/numpyro 在 Bayesian IRT 上的 convergence 表现。Parameter recovery simulation 是 psychometric model 论文的 de facto 标准。

【缺陷 6】
- 类别: 评估方案缺陷
- 问题: Proposal 中 **MT-Bench 被列为 supplementary benchmark，但对于 2026 年 frontier models，MT-Bench 存在严重的 ceiling effect**（proposal 本身也承认了 "acknowledged ceiling effects"）。问题不在于是否包含 MT-Bench，而在于：如果 ceiling effect 导致 MT-Bench 上 models 分数方差极低，MFRM 的 item difficulty 和 model ability 估计可能退化（item discrimination 趋近 0），这反而可能 **伤害** G-MFRM 的参数估计质量。包含 MT-Bench 可能需要更多的方法学讨论（如何处理 ceiling items、是否 down-weight low-discriminating items）。
- 严重度: 可补救
- 补救方案: (1) **要么将 MT-Bench 从 parameter estimation pool 中排除**（仅作为 external validation 报告 score distribution），**要么在 model estimation 时对 low-discrimination items 做 screening/down-weighting**。(2) 建议采用后者：先计算每个 item 的 point-biserial correlation 或 IRT discrimination parameter，移除 discrimination < threshold 的 items 后再拟合 G-MFRM。这是 IRT 实践中处理 ceiling effect 的标准做法，PSN-IRT 也使用了 Fisher information-based item selection。(3) 替代方案：如果 MT-Bench ceiling 太严重，考虑替换为 **Arena-Hard v2**（ArXiv:2406.11939，500 prompts，98.6% correlation with Arena）或更高难度的细分 benchmark。
- 调研依据: PSN-IRT (AAAI 2026) 使用 Fisher information-based item selection 来处理低质量 items；Arena-Hard v2 在 2026 年已更新至 98.6% correlation with Arena rankings。

【缺陷 7】
- 类别: 可行性问题
- 问题: **人工标注预算和时间线可能被低估**。Proposal 的 equivalence validation protocol 要求 "≥3 human annotators with Fleiss' κ ≥ 0.7" 对 Arena-Hard (500 prompts) 和 WildBench 的 rephrased variants 进行标注。假设每个 prompt 需要 3 annotators 验证 original + rephrased 的等价性，每个判断需 5-10 分钟（open-ended task equivalence 比 factual QA 复杂得多），500 prompts × 3 annotators × 7.5 min ≈ 187.5 person-hours，仅 Arena-Hard 就需要约 $4,700（按 $25/hr）。加上 WildBench 的 1,024 prompts，总人工成本可能达 $10,000-15,000，远超 proposal 估计的总 GPU+API 成本（$1,350-1,825）。Resource estimate 中 **完全没有提到人工标注成本**。
- 严重度: 可补救
- 补救方案: (1) **将人工标注成本纳入 resource estimate**，给出具体金额。(2) **降低标注规模**：不必对所有 500/1024 prompts 都做人工验证——可以先用 LLM-based equivalence checker 做初筛，仅对 LLM 认为等价性存疑的 top-30% items 做人工验证。(3) **分层抽样验证**：随机抽取 100-150 个 prompts 做完整 human validation，其余用 LLM-assisted checklist overlap 做 soft validation，报告抽样 sub-set 上的 Fleiss' κ 作为整体等价性的 lower bound 估计。(4) **时间线调整**：reference benchmark construction + human validation 估计 2 周可能不够，建议调整为 3 周或引入更多 annotators 并行。
- 调研依据: 基于领域实验规范判断。ConStat (NeurIPS 2024) 的 reference benchmark 基于 automatic rephrasing 无需大量人工验证（因 factual QA 的等价性容易自动判断），但 open-ended generation 的等价性验证需要更多人工参与。

【缺陷 8】
- 类别: compute 公平性问题
- 问题: Proposal 中未提到 **compute-normalized comparison**。不同 baseline 方法的计算开销差异巨大：raw average 几乎零成本，CyclicJudge 需要多 judge 推理，DCR 需要 contamination scoring pipeline，UDA 需要 neural adapter training，Bias-Bounded 需要 iterative filtering。G-MFRM 需要 3-stage estimation + reference benchmark construction。如果 G-MFRM 在 Kendall-τ 上仅比 CyclicJudge 高 0.02 但计算开销高 10x，审稿人可能质疑实际价值。Proposal 提到会报告 "efficiency-improvement tradeoff table"（非常好），但没有明确是否做 **compute-normalized ablation**（在同等 compute budget 下各方法的表现）。
- 严重度: 可补救
- 补救方案: (1) **已有的 "efficiency-improvement tradeoff table" 是很好的设计**，确保执行即可。(2) 建议补充一个 **Pareto frontier 分析**：x 轴为 compute cost (API calls + GPU hours + human annotation hours)，y 轴为 Kendall-τ，将所有方法标注在图上，展示 G-MFRM 是否在 Pareto frontier 上。(3) 明确区分 **one-time setup cost**（reference benchmark construction）和 **per-evaluation cost**（新模型加入时的 incremental cost），G-MFRM 的 amortized per-evaluation cost 可能远低于 total cost，这应该在 tradeoff table 中清晰体现。
- 调研依据: PSN-IRT (AAAI 2026) 展示了 Fisher information-based item subset selection 可在减少 70% items 的情况下保持 τ=0.9048，是 compute-quality tradeoff 分析的范例。

## Parameter Recovery Studies with Bayesian MCMC

Parameter recovery of two Bayesian estimation techniques, MCMC and VB, was investigated for different prior distribution choices using simulated data. This represents a standard practice in validating IRT models.

## Standard Validation Approaches

A comprehensive simulation study was conducted to compare parameter recovery of GPCM via MMLE and MCMC, with manipulated factors including latent distribution, sample size, and test length, and parameter recovery was evaluated with bias and root mean square error. This exemplifies how researchers typically structure parameter recovery studies.

## Prior Distribution Choices

Studies investigate the impact of three prior distributions: matched, standard vague, and hierarchical in Bayesian estimation parameter recovery in two and one parameter models. Prior selection is a critical consideration in Bayesian IRT estimation.

## Computational Methods

Bayesian estimation, especially Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) techniques, are a plausible alternative for IRT parameter estimation. Two possible reasons for the lack of adoption of Bayesian inference are (1) MCMC runs much slower than MML and (2) it is not obvious how to choose appropriate priors.

The search results indicate that simulation-based parameter recovery evaluation is well-established as standard practice in psychometric validation of IRT models using Bayesian MCMC methods.

## Small Sample Performance

Research by Long and Cliff (1997) found that tau performed reasonably well with small samples greater than 10 and less than 25, which aligns with your interest in sample sizes of 15-20.

## Statistical Power

Statistical power is the ability of a test to detect an effect if there is one, and larger sample sizes increase the power of the test, making it more likely to detect a true correlation when using Kendall's Tau. Small samples may not represent the population well, leading to a Type II error, where a true effect is missed (false negative).

## Confidence Intervals

Sample size affects the standard error of Kendall's Tau; as the sample size increases, the standard error decreases, leading to narrower confidence intervals and a more precise estimate of the correlation. With a larger sample size, the confidence intervals around Kendall's Tau become narrower, indicating a more precise estimate of the correlation coefficient.

## Bootstrap Methods

Bootstrap methods are vital for computer-intensive studies of statistical methods including simulation and Monte Carlo analysis. The search results reference functions like `kendall.ci()` that support bootstrap approaches for computing confidence intervals for Kendall's tau.

For sample sizes in the 15-20 range specifically, you may want to consult formal statistical power analyses or use simulation studies, as the bootstrap approach would be particularly useful for obtaining reliable confidence intervals in this small sample context.

## Small Sample Performance

Research by Long and Cliff (1997) found that tau performed reasonably well with small samples greater than 10 and less than 25, which aligns with your interest in sample sizes of 15-20.

## Statistical Power

Statistical power is the ability of a test to detect an effect if there is one, and larger sample sizes increase the power of the test, making it more likely to detect a true correlation when using Kendall's Tau. Small samples may not represent the population well, leading to a Type II error, where a true effect is missed (false negative).

## Confidence Intervals

Sample size affects the standard error of Kendall's Tau; as the sample size increases, the standard error decreases, leading to narrower confidence intervals and a more precise estimate of the correlation. With a larger sample size, the confidence intervals around Kendall's Tau become narrower, indicating a more precise estimate of the correlation coefficient.

Bootstrap methods are vital for computer-intensive studies of statistical methods including simulation and Monte Carlo analysis. The search results reference functions like `kendall.ci()` that support bootstrap approaches for computing confidence intervals for Kendall's tau.

【阶段】: 迭代第 2 轮

【交叉验证调研】:
1. **arXiv:2605.07046 (IRT numerical instability in LLM evaluation)** — 已验证存在。该论文明确指出 IRT 在 LLM evaluation 中面临 singular data configurations 和 numerical instability，提出 majorization-minimization 方案。补救 agent 关于 MCMC convergence 和 identifiability 的担忧有文献支撑。
2. **Parameter recovery simulation 作为 psychometric 论文标准** — 已验证。多篇 IRT 文献（Frontiers in Psychology 2016, ResearchGate parameter recovery studies）确认 simulation-based parameter recovery 是 Bayesian IRT 模型验证的 de facto 标准。补救 agent 建议合理且必要。
3. **Kendall-τ 小样本统计功效** — 已验证。Long & Cliff (1997) 研究表明 N=10-25 时 τ 表现尚可但 CIs 宽，bootstrap 方法推荐用于小样本 CI 估计。补救 agent 关于统计 power 的担忧有据，bootstrap CIs 是标准解决方案。

【发掘 agent 有效建议采纳】:
1. **发掘点 1（semi-formal confounding proposition）** — 已验证/采纳。Fiedler (arXiv:2605.06939) 的 sign-reversal 提供 empirical motivation，IRT misspecification 文献提供 formal argument 起点。将核心 claim 从 rhetoric 升级为 semi-formal result（proposition + proof sketch in appendix），这是本轮最重要的 idea 层面强化。不要求完整定理，但需要清晰的 statement + bias 方向预测。
2. **发掘点 2（paradigm shift framing）** — 部分采纳。趋势观察（ad-hoc → principled measurement）有调研支撑，但"paradigm shift"措辞过于宏大。采纳趋势定位（G-MFRM 作为 MFRM-for-raters + IRT-for-benchmarks + formal-diagnostics 三条线的自然 culmination），但不使用"paradigm shift"表述。
3. **发掘点 3（external anchoring 提升为 core contribution）** — 已验证/采纳。DG-IRT 原论文确实假设 exposure status known to administrator，这在 LLM 场景根本不成立。将 Stage 2 external anchoring 从"domain adaptation"提升为"解决 DG-IRT 在 LLM domain 的根本不可行性"的 core contribution，强化 novelty 叙事。
4. **发掘点 4（Preference Leakage 差异化）** — 已验证/采纳。Judge-side contamination (Preference Leakage) vs. examinee-side contamination (G-MFRM) 是清晰的机制差异，必须主动 articulate 以防审稿人混淆。
5. **发掘点 5（rank-1 assumption 讨论）** — 已验证/采纳。AMMI 文献中 rank 选择是标准讨论，IRT multidimensional misspecification 文献相关。主动承认 rank-1 limitation 并讨论 person-fit 检测 violation 的方法，展示 methodological maturity。不采纳扩展到 rank-k 的建议（超出论文范围），仅讨论 limitation。

【补救 agent 有效建议采纳】:
1. **缺陷 1（统计 power + controlled contamination injection）** — 已验证/采纳。Bootstrap 95% CIs 和 permutation tests 是小样本 τ 的标准做法。Controlled contamination injection（在 open-weight models 上注入已知 contamination）提供不依赖 Chatbot Arena 的 ground truth 验证，解决了 "用 contaminated ground truth 验证 decontamination" 的逻辑矛盾。DCR 和 ConStat 均采用此方法论。
2. **缺陷 2（ConStat validity study 强化）** — 已验证/部分采纳。Round 1 已加入 equivalence validation protocol，本轮追加：dedicated ConStat validity study 作为实验前置步骤、inter-indicator agreement 报告、fallback 方案（降级 ConStat 权重）。不重复 Round 1 已有内容。
3. **缺陷 3（vanilla IRT baseline）** — 已验证/采纳。PSN-IRT (AAAI 2026) 用 4PL IRT 对比 Chatbot Arena 达 τ=0.9048，是标准 IRT baseline。增加 vanilla Rasch/2PL 作为最基本参照，形成 vanilla IRT → 3-facet MFRM → G-MFRM 的清晰 ablation 梯度。UDA 转换方法说明也纳入。
4. **缺陷 4（sequential order-dependence ablation）** — 已验证/采纳。测试两种 sequential 顺序（debias→decontaminate vs. decontaminate→debias）是验证 confounding claim 的最强实验证据，直接对应 Fiedler 的 sign-reversal 发现。将 ablation (c) 扩展为三组比较。
5. **缺陷 5（MCMC convergence + parameter recovery simulation）** — 已验证/采纳。arXiv:2605.07046 确认 IRT 在 LLM 场景的 numerical challenges，parameter recovery simulation 是 psychometric 论文标准。增加 convergence diagnostic protocol（R̂ < 1.01, ESS > 400）和 synthetic data parameter recovery study。

7. **缺陷 7（人工标注成本）** — 已验证/采纳。更新 resource estimate 纳入人工标注成本，采用 LLM-assisted screening + stratified sampling（100-150 prompts 完整人工验证 + 其余 LLM-assisted）降低成本。

**Idea 层面变更：**

**实验层面变更：**
- 增加 controlled contamination injection validation（open-weight model fine-tuning 注入已知 contamination）
- 增加 bootstrap 95% CIs 和 permutation tests 用于方法间 τ 差异显著性
- 增加 vanilla Rasch/2PL baseline 形成 ablation 梯度
- 将 sequential ablation 扩展为三组比较（Sequential A: debias→decontaminate, Sequential B: decontaminate→debias, Joint G-MFRM）
- 增加 MCMC convergence diagnostic protocol 和 synthetic data parameter recovery simulation
- MT-Bench 增加 item discrimination screening
- 更新 resource estimate 纳入人工标注成本（~$3,000-5,000）和 LLM-assisted stratified sampling
- 增加 Pareto frontier 可视化（compute cost vs. τ）

【idea 质量评估】: Novelty=强 Significance=强 → idea 天花板约 48%
- Novelty 进一步强化：semi-formal confounding proposition 将贡献从 "first to integrate" 升级为 "identify and resolve a previously uncharacterized estimation pathology"；external anchoring 作为 core contribution 解决了 DG-IRT 跨域迁移的根本障碍
- Significance 稳定：填补 documented gap，interpretable multi-dimensional output，practical value for leaderboard evaluation

【实验完备性评估】: Technical Soundness=中强 → 地板已有显著提升
- Parameter recovery simulation + MCMC convergence protocol 补上了 psychometric 论文的标准要求
- Controlled contamination injection 解决了 ground truth 逻辑矛盾
- Sequential order-dependence ablation 为核心 claim 提供最强实验证据
- ConStat validity study 仍有风险但已有 fallback 方案
- 主要残留风险：ConStat 在 open-ended benchmark 上的实际 r² 未知、MCMC 在 near-ceiling data 上的实际收敛表现

【当前概率估计】: [33% - 43%] 中位 37%

【决策】: 继续

【决策理由】: 第 2 轮在 idea 层面（confounding proposition、external anchoring elevation）和实验层面（parameter recovery、controlled contamination、order-dependence ablation）均有实质性改进，中位从 35% 升至 37%。但 proposal 尚未完全收敛：(1) 发掘 agent 仍在提出实质建议（5 个发掘点中 3 个是新 angle），(2) 补救 agent 发现了 Round 1 未捕获的重要缺陷（parameter recovery simulation、statistical power、sequential order-dependence），(3) 新增内容的整合可能引入新的 inconsistency。预期第 3 轮两个 agent 都接近或到达收敛状态，届时可做最终判断。

---
# Gated Many-Facet Rasch Measurement for Joint Judge Bias and Contamination Correction in LLM Evaluation

## Description
We propose the Gated Many-Facet Rasch Model (G-MFRM), which extends the standard MFRM from educational measurement with a DG-IRT-inspired contamination gating mechanism to jointly calibrate model ability, item difficulty, judge severity, and contamination susceptibility within a single psychometric framework. The central methodological contribution is threefold. First, we identify a previously uncharacterized estimation pathology: judge severity and contamination susceptibility are confounded in sequential approaches — bias-only methods absorb contamination inflation into ability estimates, while contamination-only methods misattribute severity effects to lower contamination — and we provide a semi-formal proposition showing that sequential two-stage estimators yield asymptotically biased θ̂_n when d_j and c_n · e_i covary across items, with bias direction determined by the sign of their covariance (proof sketch in appendix; Fiedler's sign-reversal failure mode [arXiv:2605.06939] is characterized as a specific instance). Second, we design a hierarchical contamination parameterization via multiplicative gating c_n · e_i (N+I parameters), following the LLTM (Fischer 1973) / AMMI tradition with established identifiability guarantees. Third, we solve the fundamental obstacle to applying DG-IRT (Shu, Henson & Luecht, Psychometrika 2013) in the LLM domain: DG-IRT assumes exposure status is known to the test administrator, which is fundamentally inapplicable when no one knows which models saw which benchmark items during training. Our Stage 2 external anchoring pipeline — combining ConStat reference benchmark comparison (NeurIPS 2024, r²=0.94 on factual benchmarks), temporal pre/post-cutoff signals, and LogProber Safe Scores — constitutes a core methodological contribution that resolves this inapplicability, not merely an adaptation.

The DG-IRT cross-domain transfer involves three structural differences requiring new design decisions: (1) DG-IRT uses binary exposure indicators, but LLM contamination is continuous → continuous e_i; (2) DG-IRT operates in single-rater settings → MFRM d_j integration; (3) DG-IRT assumes known exposure → Stage 2 external anchoring. We acknowledge the rank-1 assumption (c_n · e_i) as a simplification: a single scalar c_n assumes homogeneous contamination susceptibility across task domains, whereas in reality a model may be highly contaminated on coding tasks but clean on reasoning tasks (e.g., due to domain-specific training data). We discuss conditions under which rank-1 is a good approximation (contamination from a single dominant data source), note that person-fit diagnostics (infit/outfit MNSQ) can detect rank-1 violations, and leave rank-k extensions to future work.

Beyond ranking correction, G-MFRM yields interpretable multi-dimensional output: c_n for training pipeline auditing, d_j for judge selection, e_i for benchmark item retirement, and b_i for difficulty calibration. It is important to distinguish G-MFRM's examinee-side contamination (model performance inflated by training on benchmark items) from Preference Leakage's (ICLR 2026, arXiv:2502.01534) judge-side contamination (judge biased by relatedness to generator): these are mechanistically distinct phenomena. Preference Leakage's relatedness bias is partially captured by G-MFRM's d_j facet when a related model serves as judge.

## Core Problem
Can a hierarchical psychometric measurement model jointly estimate model ability, item difficulty, judge severity, and contamination susceptibility — with the contamination facet decomposed into identifiable per-model and per-item components anchored by external exposure proxies — to produce bias-and-contamination-corrected evaluation scores that outperform both siloed corrections and naive sequential pipelines? Is joint estimation methodologically necessary because judge severity and contamination susceptibility are confounded in sequential approaches, as evidenced by Fiedler's (arXiv:2605.06939) sign-reversal failure mode and formalized in our confounding proposition?

## Opportunity
The LLM-as-a-judge evaluation literature has bifurcated into two silos using different formalisms and research communities: (1) judge bias correction (CyclicJudge, Bias-Bounded Evaluation, Soumik's 9-strategy comparison, UDA neural calibration, Fiedler's diagnostics) and (2) contamination detection/adjustment (DCR Factor, ConStat, Preference Leakage calibration). No existing work jointly models judge severity and contamination susceptibility within a single calibration framework. This gap is not merely organizational but methodological: sequential correction introduces estimation bias because each step cannot distinguish its target effect from the other's confounding influence. Fiedler (arXiv:2605.06939) has documented sign-reversal failure modes — a symptom of this confounding. The field is trending from ad-hoc metrics toward principled measurement frameworks — MFRM for rater effects (arXiv:2505.18486), IRT for benchmark analysis (PSN-IRT, AAAI 2026), formal diagnostics (Fiedler) — but no work yet unifies all identified measurement artifacts (judge bias, contamination, item difficulty) in a single generative model. G-MFRM provides this unification.

Recent work applying MFRM to LLM raters (arXiv:2505.18486) diagnoses rater effects only, without contamination modeling. Casabianca & Beiting-Parrish (arXiv:2602.22585) use MFRM to correct human rater effects but focus on human raters and ignore contamination. "Quantifying Data Contamination in Psychometric Evaluations of LLMs" (arXiv:2510.07175) studies contamination in psychological scales (Big Five, PVQ-40) where LLMs are test-takers — detection only, no correction, no judge modeling, distinct from our LLM-as-a-judge benchmark setting. DG-IRT (Psychometrika 2013) provides the gating mechanism but assumes administrator-known exposure, fundamentally inapplicable to LLM evaluation.

## Landscape
**Judge bias silo:** CyclicJudge (March 2026) eliminates judge bias via round-robin but ignores contamination. IRT-GRM for judge reliability (Feb 2026) diagnoses consistency without contamination modeling. Casabianca & Beiting-Parrish (arXiv:2602.22585, Feb 2026) correct human rater severity via MFRM — human raters only, no contamination. 'Judging the Judges' (Soumik, arXiv:2604.23178, April 2026) compares 9 debiasing strategies, finds style bias dominant (0.76–0.92), but explicitly lacks an explanatory measurement model. Fiedler (arXiv:2605.06939, May 2026) introduces J/delta-J diagnostics and sign-reversal failure modes, stays within classical test theory. BiasScope (ICLR 2026) automates post-hoc bias discovery. Bias-Bounded Evaluation (arXiv:2603.05485, March 2026) provides formal (τ, δ)-bias-bounded guarantees, 61–99% ranking correlation on Arena-Hard-Auto. JudgeBiasBench (March 2026): 12 bias types, 4 dimensions. UDA (AAAI 2026): neural K-factor Elo adjustment, inter-judge SD reduced 63.4%. Rogan-Gladen estimator (arXiv:2511.21140): bias correction under distribution shift for classification-based evaluation. **Contamination silo:** DCR Factor (EMNLP 2025): fuzzy inference contamination adjustment, ignores judge effects. Preference Leakage (ICLR 2026, arXiv:2502.01534): quantifies judge-side relatedness bias (generator-judge contamination), post-hoc calibration only — mechanistically distinct from examinee-side contamination modeled by G-MFRM. ConStat (NeurIPS 2024): reference benchmark comparison, r²=0.94 on factual benchmarks, fully black-box. LogProber (2024): token log-probability memorization indicators. Wang et al. (ICLR 2026): RL post-training obscures contamination signals. arXiv:2510.07175: contamination in psychological scales (detection only, no correction, no judge modeling). **IRT for LLMs:** PSN-IRT (AAAI 2026): neural 4PL IRT for benchmark evaluation, τ=0.9048 with Arena. MFRM applied to 10 LLM raters (arXiv:2505.18486) and ChatGPT-4 essay scoring (RMAL 2024). arXiv:2605.07046: identifies IRT numerical instability in LLM evaluation, proposes majorization-minimization solutions. **Gap:** No work jointly models judge severity and contamination in a single psychometric framework; DG-IRT gating never adapted to LLM contamination; sequential methods are theoretically biased due to severity-contamination confounding.

## Approach
**Why joint estimation is necessary, not merely convenient.** A naive two-stage pipeline (e.g., CyclicJudge → DCR) suffers from: (a) Bias propagation — CyclicJudge cannot distinguish genuine ability from contamination inflation, producing biased "debiased scores"; DCR then underestimates contamination for models judged by strict judges. (b) No uncertainty propagation — point estimates from step 1 enter step 2 as fixed inputs, causing confidence intervals to undercover. We formalize this as a proposition: under non-orthogonality of d_j and c_n · e_i across items, sequential estimators are asymptotically biased with bias direction determined by the covariance sign (proof sketch in appendix). Joint Bayesian estimation in a single likelihood resolves both problems.

**Model formulation.**

  logit(P_nij) = θ_n − b_i − d_j + c_n · e_i

θ_n: model ability, b_i: item difficulty, d_j: judge severity, c_n: per-model contamination susceptibility, e_i: per-item exposure level. The multiplicative gating c_n · e_i follows the LLTM (Fischer 1973) / AMMI rank-1 decomposition (N+I parameters, identifiable). When e_i ≈ 0, the model reduces to standard 3-facet MFRM; when e_i > 0, performance is inflated by c_n · e_i. Rank-1 limitation: c_n assumes domain-homogeneous contamination susceptibility; violations detectable via person-fit diagnostics (infit/outfit); rank-k extensions left to future work.

**Three-stage estimation.**

*Stage 1 — Standard 3-facet MFRM:* Fit θ_n, b_i, d_j via Bayesian MCMC (NumPyro), ignoring contamination. Produces initial estimates and person-fit statistics (lz, EMRi).

*Stage 2 — External exposure estimation (core contribution resolving DG-IRT inapplicability):* DG-IRT assumes administrator-known exposure — inapplicable when no one knows which models saw which benchmark items. We estimate e_i from external proxies independent of the MFRM fit:
  (a) ConStat delta scores (black-box, r²=0.94 on factual benchmarks). # Gated Many-Facet Rasch Measurement for Joint Judge Bias and Contamination Correction in LLM Evaluation

## Description
We propose the Gated Many-Facet Rasch Model (G-MFRM), which extends the standard MFRM from educational measurement with a DG-IRT-inspired contamination gating mechanism to jointly calibrate model ability, item difficulty, judge severity, and contamination susceptibility within a single psychometric framework. The central methodological contribution is threefold. First, we identify a previously uncharacterized estimation pathology: judge severity and contamination susceptibility are confounded in sequential approaches — bias-only methods absorb contamination inflation into ability estimates, while contamination-only methods misattribute severity effects to lower contamination — and we provide a semi-formal proposition showing that sequential two-stage estimators yield asymptotically biased θ̂_n when d_j and c_n · e_i covary across items, with bias direction determined by the sign of their covariance (proof sketch in appendix; Fiedler's sign-reversal failure mode [arXiv:2605.06939] is characterized as a specific instance). Second, we design a hierarchical contamination parameterization via multiplicative gating c_n · e_i (N+I parameters), following the LLTM (Fischer 1973) / AMMI tradition with established identifiability guarantees. Third, we solve the fundamental obstacle to applying DG-IRT (Shu, Henson & Luecht, Psychometrika 2013) in the LLM domain: DG-IRT assumes exposure status is known to the test administrator, which is fundamentally inapplicable when no one knows which models saw which benchmark items during training. Our Stage 2 external anchoring pipeline — combining ConStat reference benchmark comparison (NeurIPS 2024, r²=0.94 on factual benchmarks), temporal pre/post-cutoff signals, and LogProber Safe Scores — constitutes a core methodological contribution that resolves this inapplicability, not merely an adaptation.

The DG-IRT cross-domain transfer involves three structural differences requiring new design decisions: (1) DG-IRT uses binary exposure indicators, but LLM contamination is continuous → continuous e_i; (2) DG-IRT operates in single-rater settings → MFRM d_j integration; (3) DG-IRT assumes known exposure → Stage 2 external anchoring. We acknowledge the rank-1 assumption (c_n · e_i) as a simplification: a single scalar c_n assumes homogeneous contamination susceptibility across task domains, whereas in reality a model may be highly contaminated on coding tasks but clean on reasoning tasks (e.g., due to domain-specific training data). We discuss conditions under which rank-1 is a good approximation (contamination from a single dominant data source), note that person-fit diagnostics (infit/outfit MNSQ) can detect rank-1 violations, and leave rank-k extensions to future work.

Beyond ranking correction, G-MFRM yields interpretable multi-dimensional output: c_n for training pipeline auditing, d_j for judge selection, e_i for benchmark item retirement, and b_i for difficulty calibration. It is important to distinguish G-MFRM's examinee-side contamination (model performance inflated by training on benchmark items) from Preference Leakage's (ICLR 2026, arXiv:2502.01534) judge-side contamination (judge biased by relatedness to generator): these are mechanistically distinct phenomena. Preference Leakage's relatedness bias is partially captured by G-MFRM's d_j facet when a related model serves as judge.

## Core Problem
Can a hierarchical psychometric measurement model jointly estimate model ability, item difficulty, judge severity, and contamination susceptibility — with the contamination facet decomposed into identifiable per-model and per-item components anchored by external exposure proxies — to produce bias-and-contamination-corrected evaluation scores that outperform both siloed corrections and naive sequential pipelines? Is joint estimation methodologically necessary because judge severity and contamination susceptibility are confounded in sequential approaches, as evidenced by Fiedler's (arXiv:2605.06939) sign-reversal failure mode and formalized in our confounding proposition?

## Opportunity
The LLM-as-a-judge evaluation literature has bifurcated into two silos using different formalisms and research communities: (1) judge bias correction (CyclicJudge, Bias-Bounded Evaluation, Soumik's 9-strategy comparison, UDA neural calibration, Fiedler's diagnostics) and (2) contamination detection/adjustment (DCR Factor, ConStat, Preference Leakage calibration). No existing work — including all arXiv submissions through May 2026 and ICLR/EMNLP 2026 proceedings — jointly models judge severity and contamination susceptibility within a single calibration framework. This gap is not merely organizational but methodological: sequential correction introduces estimation bias because each step cannot distinguish its target effect from the other's confounding influence. Fiedler (arXiv:2605.06939) has documented sign-reversal failure modes — a symptom of this confounding. The field is trending from ad-hoc metrics toward principled measurement frameworks — MFRM for rater effects (arXiv:2505.18486), IRT for benchmark analysis (PSN-IRT, AAAI 2026), formal diagnostics (Fiedler) — but no work yet unifies all identified measurement artifacts (judge bias, contamination, item difficulty) in a single generative model. G-MFRM provides this unification.

Recent work applying MFRM to LLM raters (arXiv:2505.18486) diagnoses rater effects only, without contamination modeling. Casabianca & Beiting-Parrish (arXiv:2602.22585) use MFRM to correct human rater effects but focus on human raters and ignore contamination. "Quantifying Data Contamination in Psychometric Evaluations of LLMs" (arXiv:2510.07175) studies contamination in psychological scales (Big Five, PVQ-40) where LLMs are test-takers — detection only, no correction, no judge modeling, distinct from our LLM-as-a-judge benchmark setting. DG-IRT (Psychometrika 2013) provides the gating mechanism but assumes administrator-known exposure, fundamentally inapplicable to LLM evaluation.

## Landscape
**Judge bias silo:** CyclicJudge (March 2026) eliminates judge bias via round-robin but ignores contamination. IRT-GRM for judge reliability (Feb 2026) diagnoses consistency without contamination modeling. Casabianca & Beiting-Parrish (arXiv:2602.22585, Feb 2026) correct human rater severity via MFRM — human raters only, no contamination. 'Judging the Judges' (Soumik, arXiv:2604.23178, April 2026) compares 9 debiasing strategies, finds style bias dominant (0.76–0.92), but explicitly lacks an explanatory measurement model. Fiedler (arXiv:2605.06939, May 2026) introduces J/delta-J diagnostics and sign-reversal failure modes, stays within classical test theory. BiasScope (ICLR 2026) automates post-hoc bias discovery. Bias-Bounded Evaluation (arXiv:2603.05485, March 2026) provides formal (τ, δ)-bias-bounded guarantees, 61–99% ranking correlation on Arena-Hard-Auto. Rogan-Gladen estimator (arXiv:2511.21140): bias correction under distribution shift for classification-based evaluation. **Contamination silo:** DCR Factor (EMNLP 2025): fuzzy inference contamination adjustment, ignores judge effects. ConStat (NeurIPS 2024): reference benchmark comparison, r²=0.94 on factual benchmarks, fully black-box. LogProber (2024): token log-probability memorization indicators. Wang et al. MFRM applied to 10 LLM raters (arXiv:2505.18486) and ChatGPT-4 essay scoring (RMAL 2024). arXiv:2605.07046: identifies IRT numerical instability in LLM evaluation, proposes majorization-minimization solutions. **Gap:** No work jointly models judge severity and contamination in a single psychometric framework; DG-IRT gating never adapted to LLM contamination; sequential methods are theoretically biased due to severity-contamination confounding.

## Approach
**Why joint estimation is necessary, not merely convenient.** A naive two-stage pipeline (e.g., CyclicJudge → DCR) suffers from: (a) Bias propagation — CyclicJudge cannot distinguish genuine ability from contamination inflation, producing biased "debiased scores"; DCR then underestimates contamination for models judged by strict judges. (b) No uncertainty propagation — point estimates from step 1 enter step 2 as fixed inputs, causing confidence intervals to undercover. We formalize this as a proposition: under non-orthogonality of d_j and c_n · e_i across items, sequential estimators are asymptotically biased with bias direction determined by the covariance sign (proof sketch in appendix). Joint Bayesian estimation in a single likelihood resolves both problems.

**Model formulation.**

  logit(P_nij) = θ_n − b_i − d_j + c_n · e_i

θ_n: model ability, b_i: item difficulty, d_j: judge severity, c_n: per-model contamination susceptibility, e_i: per-item exposure level. The multiplicative gating c_n · e_i follows the LLTM (Fischer 1973) / AMMI rank-1 decomposition (N+I parameters, identifiable). When e_i ≈ 0, the model reduces to standard 3-facet MFRM; when e_i > 0, performance is inflated by c_n · e_i. Rank-1 limitation: c_n assumes domain-homogeneous contamination susceptibility; violations detectable via person-fit diagnostics (infit/outfit); rank-k extensions left to future work.

**Three-stage estimation.**

*Stage 1 — Standard 3-facet MFRM:* Fit θ_n, b_i, d_j via Bayesian MCMC (NumPyro), ignoring contamination. Produces initial estimates and person-fit statistics (lz, EMRi).

*Stage 2 — External exposure estimation (core contribution resolving DG-IRT inapplicability):* DG-IRT assumes administrator-known exposure — inapplicable when no one knows which models saw which benchmark items. We estimate e_i from external proxies independent of the MFRM fit:

  (b) Temporal signals: pre/post-cutoff performance gaps.
  (c) LogProber Safe Scores (gray-box, for models exposing logprobs).
  Weighted composite produces ê_i. Inter-indicator agreement (ConStat vs. temporal vs. LogProber correlation) reported. Person-fit statistics from Stage 1 serve as validation only (not used in estimation).

*Stage 3 — Joint Gated MFRM:* Refit full model with ê_i fixed, c_n latent, Stage 1 priors. Constraints: sum(c_n) = 0, ê_i scale fixed from Stage 2. Yields fair scores θ̂_n.

**MCMC convergence and identifiability protocol.** Convergence diagnostics: R̂ < 1.01, ESS > 400 for all parameters, trace plots, posterior predictive checks. Parameter recovery simulation on synthetic data with known ground-truth (θ_n, b_i, d_j, c_n, e_i): report mean absolute error and 95% credible interval coverage. Boundary conditions tested: low-contamination (e_i ≈ 0), low c_n variance, small N (≤10 models). IRT numerical instability considerations per arXiv:2605.07046 addressed via informative priors and Stage 1 warm-starting.

**N-gram overlap.** Dropped for proprietary models. Supplementary validation for open-weight models (DeepSeek-V4, Kimi K2.6, Qwen3, Llama 4).
